restored_sea_1112._r5: G-below6-sea-r4-stronghold: r4 fixed the sunset (S3/S4 +0.53, 3/3) but the row went level because the restoration no longer read on S1/S2; r1 read there (+0.67) with deeper water. r5 gives each time of day its own values: at the day preset the shallow band draws in to a quarter of the live reach with calmer waves (the deeper, calmer restored channel of r1, with the live colours kept), at every other preset the r4 values; and in both the surf on the sandbars is stronger and reaches further (shoreline foam, asked for 3/3).
restored_sea_1112._r4: GPU pre-check on r3: S4 sunset restored foreground still near black (L 25 -> 20, black share 70 -> 80 percent). Every value r1-r3 lowered darkens low-sun water (a narrower shallow band, calmer waves, clearer shallows). r4 goes the other way: the shallow colour reaches 1.3 times further (restored shallows), the waves ease to 0.8, and alpha is left alone.
restored_sea_1112._r2: G-below6-restored-sea (SPLIT: S1/S2 row +0.67 3/3, S3/S4 -0.44 0/3): the absolute depth falloff (2.2 against a live profile of 16 or more) and deeper colour turned the sunset foreground near-black and thinned the day turquoise. r2 keeps the live colours, halves the live depth falloff so the shoal rings still show, and eases the waves instead of halving them.
